- Neuromed gets the verifiable evidence you need for internal auditors.
- Avoids production snapshot transfers that create IP and operational risk.
- Keeps operator credentials controlled (we offer temporary session tokens + audit logging).

Elena —

Great questions — short answers below and I've attached an updated schedule and small redline set that addresses these points. See RN-PrivDeploy-redlines.docx (changes highlighted).

1) Audit logs and historical operator actions: yes — we can provide cryptographically-signed audit log extracts for the requested 30‑day window. These are delivered as hashed manifests + raw log extracts over S3 with checksum, and the attestation PDF will reference the manifest checksums for chain-of-custody.

2) Session recording: we are happy to allow recording on your side. Our standard ask is that any recorded sessions remain encrypted and only used for internal audit purposes; Redwood will retain session metadata (who accessed, start/stop, session token id) but not the recording. We can add a one‑line confirmation to the runbook.

3) Session token mechanics: tokens are TTL'd (default 4 hours), revocable immediately by an RBAC action, and we support a two‑approver gating workflow for sessions as an optional control. We'll call this out in the runbook and in the new Audit Exhibit.

Next steps: If Neuromed's legal is comfortable with the alternate path, I'll open a DocuSign envelope for the single exhibit swap (link below). If you prefer an on‑site snapshot as a fallback, we propose a narrowly-scoped, technical-only snapshot under a mutual escrow governance document — but it is our preference to avoid that unless required.

DocuSign (proposed): https://docusign.example.com/templates/privdeploy-attestation
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ND-2026-0928
Jira: JIRA-1452 (audit-runbook workstream)

I've also attached evidence_schedule_v1.xlsx with tentative dates; please propose 2‑3 windows that work for your auditors.
